comparisons.peer_summary: AMD continued investing in the open ROCm software stack, making key optimizations and adding features in the latest release to improve performance for generative AI workloads and simplify the developer experience.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose specific software ecosystem investments targeting the generative AI market. AVGO focuses on a 'Private AI' solution that allows organizations to deploy generative AI while managing privacy and compliance. Similarly, AMD details its investment in the 'ROCm open software stack,' making optimizations specifically for 'highly-performant AI training and inference' and 'generative AI workloads.' While AVGO emphasizes the enterprise privacy/compliance aspect of on-premise or private deployment, AMD emphasizes the open software performance and developer experience for generative AI workloads.

sentences.text: • Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.

We continued to invest in driving software capabilities and the open ecosystem to deliver powerful new features and capabilities in the AMD ROCm™ open software stack, bringing the latest features to highly-performant AI training and inference on AMD platforms.

During the year, we made several key optimizations and additional features in the latest AMD ROCm software that increases performance in key generative AI workloads, adds expanded support and optimization for additional frameworks and libraries, and simplifies the overall developer experience.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight software strategy as a key enabler for their AI hardware offerings. AVGO describes its 'Private AI' solution as enabling organizations to use generative AI technologies, implying a software-defined approach to deployment. Intel explicitly describes its strategy of optimizing AI frameworks (like PyTorch, TensorFlow) and contributing to open standards (oneAPI, OpenVINO) to run efficiently on its hardware. Both disclosures underscore the importance of software ecosystems and toolkits in realizing the value of AI infrastructure, with AVGO focusing on the 'Private AI' solution set and Intel focusing on open-source framework optimization and middleware.

sentences.text: • Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.
We aim to optimize AI frameworks and middleware, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, vLLM, Hugging Face and WebNN to run efficiently on our hardware.

Our OpenVINO™ toolkit is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on our processors across various use cases, such as generative AI, computer vision, audio, and language with industry standard models.

Most of these frameworks and middleware are built from our oneAPI, which enables developers to create performant cross-architecture applications using a single code base across CPUs, GPUs, and other accelerators.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI and High-Performance Storage Offerings
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for AI and big data is driving the need for high-performance storage; SBU addresses this with the 6500 30TB SSD for AI data lakes and sampled the 9550 series in 2024 for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU identify generative AI and big data as primary demand drivers for their respective infrastructure components. AVGO’s 'Private AI' solution enables organizations to handle generative AI workloads, which inherently require robust data processing and storage. MU explicitly states that 'growing use of cloud computing and big data analytics is fueling the demand for high performance storage' and notes that 'machine learning servers require fast access to data.' MU addresses this with SSDs for 'AI data lake applications,' while AVGO provides the software solution layer for 'generative AI technologies.' Both disclosures reflect the infrastructure build-out required for AI workloads.

sentences.text: • Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.
Data center: The growing use of cloud computing and big data analytics is fueling the demand for high performance storage in data centers.
Our 6500 30TB SSDs features high performance, reliability, and endurance for AI data lake applications.

comparisons.peer_summary: Professional artists and designers use NVIDIA partner products for creative use cases, while generative AI expands the market for workstation-class GPUs as enterprises deploy AI applications on-premises.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the expansion of generative AI markets into enterprise settings. AVGO notes that its 'Private AI' solution enables organizations to use generative AI while addressing privacy needs, often implying on-premises or private cloud deployment. NVIDIA similarly notes that 'generative AI is expanding the market for our workstation-class GPUs, as more enterprise customers develop and deploy AI applications with their data on-premises.' Both disclosures highlight the trend of enterprises adopting AI capabilities locally to control data and privacy, driving demand for AVGO's software solutions and NVIDIA's hardware/software platforms.

sentences.text: • Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.
In addition, generative AI is expanding the market for our workstation-class GPUs, as more enterprise customers develop and deploy AI applications with their data on-premises.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm believes generative AI use cases must run on-device to maximize utility by bringing immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization benefits to consumers.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and QCOM emphasize privacy and security as critical benefits of their respective generative AI approaches, though at different layers of the stack. AVGO’s 'Private AI' solution is explicitly designed to 'address privacy and compliance needs of the organization.' QCOM argues that generative AI use cases 'must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization.' Both disclosures align on the premise that keeping AI processing local (whether in the enterprise data center for AVGO or on the edge device for QCOM) is a key value proposition driven by privacy concerns.

sentences.text: • Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.

While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.
